name: Pasta in Red Sauce (Indian-style)
cuisine: Italian-Indian fusion (cafe and home-kitchen tomato pasta, popular across India)

ingredients.name: Cooking oil (olive oil, or any neutral oil)

equipment: Medium pot (2 L) with a lid
Measuring spoons and a cup (a steel tumbler and normal teaspoon are fine stand-ins)

steps.title: Measure the penne
steps.text: Put 75 g (about ¾ cup) dry penne in a bowl.
steps.visualCue: Pale yellow, dry, hard tubes with no broken crumbs
steps.videoShot: Penne poured from a packet into a steel bowl.
steps.watchOut: Guessing the amount; dry penne almost doubles in size, so 1 cup dry becomes a very large plate. Weigh it or use a ¾ cup measure.

steps.title: Blend the tomatoes
steps.text: Cut 2 medium tomatoes (150 g) into quarters and blend with no water until smooth.
steps.visualCue: A thick, smooth, bright red puree with no big skin pieces left
steps.cameraCheck: The jar of red tomato puree
steps.videoShot: Tomato quarters turning into red puree in the mixer jar.
steps.watchOut: Adding water; the sauce then takes much longer to thicken and tastes thin. If it is already watery, cook it a few minutes longer in step 13.

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: Pour 750 ml water into the pot, cover and put it on high heat.
steps.tip: A lid brings the water to a boil much faster.
steps.visualCue: Big bubbles rise from the bottom and keep breaking across the surface (a rolling boil); steam pushes at the lid
steps.videoShot: Top-down shot of water coming to a rolling boil.
steps.watchOut: Adding pasta to water that is only warm; the penne turns sticky and soft outside while raw inside. Wait until the bubbles are large and constant.

steps.title: Salt the water
steps.text: Add 1 level tsp (5 g) salt to the boiling water.
steps.visualCue: The water fizzes up for a second, then settles back to a boil
steps.cameraCheck: The tsp of salt over the pot
steps.watchOut: Skipping the salt; the penne tastes flat and no amount of sauce fixes it. More than 1 tsp for this amount makes the plate too salty.

steps.title: Add the penne
steps.text: Tip in the penne and stir once.
steps.visualCue: The tubes sink, the boiling pauses and then returns within a minute
steps.videoShot: Penne sliding into the boiling pot.
steps.watchOut: Penne stuck together or to the bottom; this is seen as clumps when you lift the spoon. Stir for the first 30 seconds and the clumps loosen.

steps.title: Cook the penne
steps.text: Keep it at a steady boil, uncovered, stirring now and then, for 9-10 minutes (about 1 minute less than the packet says).
steps.tip: Chop the onion and garlic (step 9) while the penne cooks.
steps.visualCue: Penne swells and turns a lighter, slightly glossy yellow; a bitten piece is firm with a thin white dot in the centre (al dente)
steps.cameraCheck: One penne piece bitten in half, showing the centre
steps.videoShot: Penne bobbing in rolling water, then one piece bitten.
steps.watchOut: Overcooking; the tubes split open and feel mushy, and they get softer again in the sauce. Taste one at 8 minutes and drain when it still has a little bite.

steps.title: Save the pasta water
steps.text: Scoop out 60 ml (4 tbsp) of the cloudy water in a cup.
steps.visualCue: The water in the cup is cloudy and a little milky from starch
steps.videoShot: A cup dipped into the pasta pot.
steps.watchOut: Draining first and forgetting; the sauce later turns dry and clumpy. If you forgot, use 60 ml plain hot water, though it binds a little less well.

steps.title: Drain the penne
steps.text: Pour the pot through the colander and shake once. Do not rinse.
steps.visualCue: Steam rises, the penne is glossy and the water runs out clear
steps.videoShot: Steam rising as penne is drained.
steps.watchOut: Rinsing with cold water; it washes off the starch and the sauce slides off the pasta. If the penne sticks together while waiting, toss with 1 tsp of the saved water.

steps.title: Chop the onion and garlic
steps.text: Finely chop 40 g onion and 5 g (2 small cloves) garlic.
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces, about the size of a grain of rice
steps.cameraCheck: Chopped onion and garlic on the board
steps.videoShot: Knife chopping onion into small cubes.
steps.watchOut: Large garlic pieces; they stay raw-tasting or burn while the onion cooks. Chop garlic finer than the onion.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the pan on medium heat and add 2 tsp (9 g) oil.
steps.visualCue: The oil looks thin and shimmers; a small piece of onion dropped in sizzles gently
steps.watchOut: Smoking oil; it smells acrid and the garlic will burn at once. If it smokes, take the pan off the heat for 20 seconds.

steps.title: Fry the garlic
steps.tip: Keep the heat at medium-low, and add the onion the moment the garlic smells good.
steps.visualCue: Garlic turns pale gold and smells sweet and sharp
steps.watchOut: Brown or black garlic, which tastes bitter. If it browns, wash the pan and start again; it will taint the whole plate.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Add the onion and cook, stirring.
steps.visualCue: Onion turns soft and see-through (translucent), with a sweet smell, and only a hint of gold at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The soft onion in the pan
steps.watchOut: Dark brown onion; the sauce turns brownish and loses its bright red colour. Lower the heat if the edges start to colour (Sharmi's Passions fries to golden; keep it lighter here).

steps.title: Cook the tomato puree
steps.text: Pour in the tomato puree and add 1 g (½ tsp) chilli powder and 1.5 g (a scant ¼ tsp) salt. Stir and cook on medium-low.
steps.visualCue: The puree darkens from bright to deep red, thickens so a spoon leaves a trail, tiny oil droplets show at the edge, and the raw tomato smell turns sweet
steps.cameraCheck: The thick red sauce in the pan
steps.videoShot: Red puree bubbling slowly with oil at the edges.
steps.watchOut: Splatter and a sour, raw taste. The puree spits on high heat, so keep the heat low and half-cover; if it still tastes sharp, cook 2 minutes more or add a pinch of sugar.

steps.title: Add the flavourings
steps.text: Stir in 1 g (½ tsp) chilli flakes, 1 g (½ tsp) mixed herbs, a pinch of pepper and 10 g (2 tsp) ketchup.
steps.visualCue: Green and red flecks spread through the sauce, the colour turns a little glossier and the smell turns herby
steps.watchOut: Burning the herbs on a hot pan, which turns them bitter. Add them with the heat low.

steps.title: Toss in the penne
steps.text: Add the drained penne and 60 ml (4 tbsp) pasta water. Toss on low heat.
steps.visualCue: The sauce thins slightly, turns glossy and clings to the ridges and inside the tubes; no puddle of loose sauce is left
steps.cameraCheck: The pasta coated in red sauce
steps.videoShot: Penne tossed in the red sauce.
steps.watchOut: A dry, sticky plate (add 1 tbsp more pasta water) or a watery one (cook 30 seconds longer on low heat). Stir gently; rough mixing breaks the tubes.

steps.title: Plate and serve
steps.text: Move to a warm plate, taste and add a little salt only if needed. Top with 15 g grated cheese if you want it (optional, not counted).
steps.visualCue: Glossy red penne with green and red flecks, steaming
steps.watchOut: Waiting; the sauce is absorbed as the pasta cools and the plate turns dry and stiff. Serve at once; loosen with a splash of hot water if it thickens.

reasons: about 12 g protein and 6 g fibre from a plate of refined durum pasta, with only 2 tsp oil, no cream or cheese, no cholesterol and low saturated fat (about 1.5 g). Points off for refined pasta, about 900 mg sodium (45% of the limit), and few vegetables. Restaurant plates are often a larger pasta portion with more oil, ketchup or cream, cheese and salt, and garlic bread on the side (est.).

researchRating.basis: a very widely made home and cafe pasta in India, with many Indian recipes (Sharmi's Passions, Tarla Dalal, Chitra's Food Book, Hebbar's Kitchen, Cookinsta) and the classic Italian arrabbiata behind it. Points off because no star-rating figure or review comments could be read from this environment (only search snippets), because the plain version is rated as basic compared with creamy pink or white sauce pasta, and because Tarla Dalal notes the recipe uses refined flour and is not recommended for weight loss.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days (est.); not recommended for the freezer (cooked pasta turns soft on thawing, est.). Reheat in a pan on low heat with 2-3 tbsp of water, stirring, until steaming; the sauce thickens when cold.
leftoverRemix: Masala pasta tikki. Mash leftover pasta with 1 tbsp besan and a pinch of chaat masala, shape into a small patty and shallow-fry in 1 tsp oil on a tawa for 3 minutes a side until crisp and golden. Not recommended if the pasta was stored more than 2 days.
burnOff: about 6.1 km of running (425 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 8.5 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 42 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: wheat pasta is outside the common vrat rule set (kuttu, rajgira, singhara, samvat), and the recipe has onion, garlic and table salt.

ekadashi.reason: grains are avoided on Ekadashi in the common rule set; the recipe also has onion and garlic.

jain.reason: drop onion and garlic (see Jain variant).

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; suits iftar, and is lighter than a cream pasta (about 425 kcal, about 900 mg sodium); fine for sehri if you want a carbohydrate-rich meal, though the chilli flakes may be too sharp for some.

jain.reason: onion and garlic are root vegetables; drop both and use a pinch of gluten-free hing and dry ginger powder (sonth) (see Jain variant). Tomato is kept; strictness about tomato varies by household (single rule not confirmed here).

vegan.reason: no dairy, ghee, honey, egg or meat in the recipe (oil, tomato, onion, spices, ketchup). Dried penne is normally egg-free, but check the pack (fresh pasta often has egg); skip the optional cheese topping.

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, fish or egg in the recipe.

sattvik.reason: skip the 40 g onion and 5 g garlic (see Sattvik variant).

glutenFree.reason: penne is wheat; use gluten-free penne (rice, corn or chickpea) (see Gluten-free variant). No hing is used in the main recipe.

dairyFree.reason: no dairy in the recipe; only the optional cheese topping is dairy and it is left out of the count.
